Tafsir of Surat "Nun wal-Qalam" (Makkiyya according to al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir). Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: from its beginning up to His saying, the Exalted, "We shall brand him upon the snout" (al-Qalam: [[verse (16)]] [16]) is Makki. From after that up to His saying, "Greater, if they only knew" (al-Qalam: [[verse (33)]] [33]) is Madani. From after that up to His saying, "they write" (al-Qalam: [[verse (47)]] [47]) is Makki. From after that up to His saying, "of the righteous" ([[verse 50]] [al-Qalam: 50]) is Madani, and what remains is Makki. This is what al-Mawardi said.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe (1). You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman (2). And indeed for you is a reward never cut off (3).

His saying, the Exalted: "Nun. By the pen." Abu Bakr, al-Mufaddal, Hubayrah, Warsh, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Amir, al-Kisai and Ya'qub assimilated (idgham) the second nun into the letter waw in its spelling (hija'). The rest recited with clear pronunciation (izhar). Isa ibn Umar read it with a fatha, as if he had supposed a verb. Ibn Abbas, Nasr and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra, by supposing the particle of oath (harf al-qasam). Harun and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa read it with a damma, as an indeclinable form (al-bina').

Its interpretation has been disputed. Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah reported from his father, traced back to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Nun" is (a tablet of light). Thabit al-Bunani reported that Nun is the inkwell (al-dawah); this is also said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Al-Walid ibn Muslim reported, saying: Malik ibn Anas narrated to us from Sumayy, client of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. That is the saying of the Exalted: 'Nun. By the pen.' Then He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'What has been and what will be until the Day of Resurrection, of deed, term, provision or trace.' So the pen ran with what will be until the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Then He sealed the mouth of the pen, so it does not speak and will not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect, and the Almighty said: 'I have not created a creature more wondrous to Me than you. By My might and My majesty, I shall perfect you in those whom I love, and I shall diminish you in those whom I hate.'" He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most complete of people in intellect are the most obedient of them to Allah and the most active in His obedience."

From Mujahid, who said: Nun is the fish beneath the seventh earth. He said: "And the pen" is the one with which the Remembrance was written. Likewise said Muqatil, Murrah al-Hamdani, Ata al-Khurasani, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi: that the nun is the fish upon which the earths rest.

Abu Zabyan reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and it ran with what will be. Then He raised the vapour of water and created the heaven from it. Then He created the nun and spread the earth upon its back. The earth shook, so it was steadied with mountains, and indeed the mountains boast over the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited: "Nun. By the pen," the verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: its name is al-Bahmut [[al-Alusi, in his tafsir, vocalised it as "al-yahmut" with a voweled initial yā' and a sukun on the hā'.]]. The rajaz poet said:

"Why do I see you all silent...
Allah, my Lord, created the Bahmut."

Abu al-Yaqzan and al-Waqidi said: "luyuthan." Ka'b said: "luthuthan." He also said: "Balahmuthan." [[The manuscripts and references available to us vary greatly in these names. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, departed from what he stipulated in the introduction to his book, p. (3), where he said: "...and I set aside much of the stories of the exegetes and the reports of historians..." etc.]] Ka'b also said: Iblis penetrated to the fish upon whose back rest the earths and whispered into its heart, saying: "Do you know what is upon your back, O Luthuthan, of animals, trees, earths and others? If you were to vomit them, you would cast them all off your back." So he resolved to do that, and Allah sent to him a creature which entered his nostril and reached his brain. The fish cried out to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because of it, so Allah permitted it and it came out. Ka'b said: "By Allah, it looks at it and it looks at it; if it intends anything of that, it returns as it was."

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas: that "Nun" is the last letter of the letters of "al-Rahman." He said: "Ra", "Lam-ha" and "Nun" are the letters of "al-Rahman" the Exalted, separated. Ibn Zayd said: it is an oath which the Exalted swore by. Ibn Kaysan said: it is the opening of the surah. It is also said: it is the name of the surah. Ata and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the initial of His name Nasir, Nur and Nasir. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His support for the believers, and it is true. Its explanation is the saying of the Exalted: "And it was ever incumbent upon Us to aid the believers" [al-Rum: 47] [[See vol. 14, p. 43]]. Ja'far al-Sadiq said: it is a river from the rivers of Paradise called Nun. It has also been said: it is the well-known letter of the alphabet, for if it were otherwise it would be declinable. This is the view chosen by al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim in his tafsir. He said: "Because Nun is a letter which is not declined; had it been a complete word, it would be declined as al-Qalam is declined. So it is therefore a letter of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hijaʾ), as in all the openings of the surahs." On this basis it has been said: it is the name of the surah, i.e., this surah is Nun.

Then he said: "By the pen": He swore by the pen because of the clarity it contains, like the tongue. It applies to every pen with which those in the heavens and those on earth write. From it is the saying of Abu al-Fath al-Busti:

"When champions swear one day by their swords,
and count them among what earns glory and nobility,
The pens of scribes suffice for honour and elevation
for all time, that Allah swore by the pen."

There are many verses of poets preferring the pen to the sword; what we have mentioned is the highest of them. Ibn Abbas said: this is an oath by the pen which Allah created; He commanded it, and it ran writing all that will be until the Day of Resurrection. He said: It is a pen of light, its length as the distance between heaven and earth. It is also said: Allah created the pen, then looked at it, and it split into two halves. He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what will be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet. Al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: My father advised me at his death, saying: "O my son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Him, nor attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in destiny, its good and its evil. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran at that very hour with what was and what will be until eternity.'" Ibn Abbas said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what will be, so it wrote among what it wrote: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab" [al-Masad: 1]. So Allah, the Exalted, sent down in reply to them and in refutation of their saying: "You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman," that is, by the mercy of your Lord. The grace here is mercy. It is also possible that "by the grace" is an oath; its sense being: "You and the grace of your Lord are not mad," because the waw and the ba are particles of oath. It has also been said: it is like your saying: "You are not mad, and praise be to Allah." It has also been said: its meaning is "You are not mad, and the grace belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise," meaning "and praise belongs to Allah." From it is the saying of Labid:

"I was left alone in the world after the loss of my kinsfolk,
and a neighbour in Arbad, a beneficial one, departed from me."

That is, "and he is Arbad." Al-Nabigha said:

"They were not deprived of the goodness of nourishment, and their mother
overflowed upon you with a male-begetting milk-bag."

That is, "he is the one who bears." The ba in "by the grace of your Lord" is connected to "madman" negated, just as it is connected to "heedless" affirmed, as in your saying: "You are heedless of the grace of your Lord." Its position is accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), as if he said: "You are not mad, one who has been favoured with that."

"And indeed for you is a reward": that is, a recompense for what you have borne of the burdens of prophethood.

"Never cut off" (ghayra mamnun): that is, not cut off and not diminished. It is said: "I cut the rope" (mantu al-habl) when I severed it, and a rope is called "manin" when it is not strong. The poet said:

"grey, swift birds whose food is not cut off [[This is the second half of a line by Labid; its first half is disputed. See the root (m-t-n) in Lisan al-Arab. The ghubs is the colour of ashes.]]"

That is, is not cut off. Mujahid said: "never cut off" means "counted" (mahsub). Al-Hasan said: "never cut off" means not spoiled by reproach. Al-Dahhak said: a reward without work. It has also been said: "not measured," which is grace (al-tafaddul), because recompense is measured and grace is not measured; this was mentioned by al-Mawardi, and it is the meaning of Mujahid's saying.

Its explanation is the saying of the Exalted: "And it was ever incumbent upon Us to aid the believers" [al-Rum: 47] [[See vol. 14, p. 43]]. Ja'far al-Sadiq said: it is a river from the rivers of Paradise called Nun. It has also been said: it is the well-known letter of the alphabet, for if it were otherwise it would be declinable. This is the view chosen by al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim in his tafsir. He said: "Because Nun is a letter which is not declined; had it been a complete word, it would be declined as al-Qalam is declined. So it is therefore a letter of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hijaʾ), as in all the openings of the surahs." On this basis it has been said: it is the name of the surah, i.e., this surah is Nun.

Then he said: "By the pen": He swore by the pen because of the clarity it contains, like the tongue. It applies to every pen with which those in the heavens and those on earth write. From it is the saying of Abu al-Fath al-Busti:

"When champions swear one day by their swords,
and count them among what earns glory and nobility,
The pens of scribes suffice for honour and elevation
for all time, that Allah swore by the pen."

There are many verses of poets preferring the pen to the sword; what we have mentioned is the highest of them. Ibn Abbas said: this is an oath by the pen which Allah created; He commanded it, and it ran writing all that will be until the Day of Resurrection. He said: It is a pen of light, its length as the distance between heaven and earth. It is also said: Allah created the pen, then looked at it, and it split into two halves. He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what will be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet. Al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: My father advised me at his death, saying: "O my son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Him, nor attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in destiny, its good and its evil. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran at that very hour with what was and what will be until eternity.'" Ibn Abbas said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what will be, so it wrote among what it wrote: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab" [al-Masad: 1]. Qatadah said: The pen is a blessing from Allah upon His servants. Others said: Allah created the first pen and it wrote what will occur in the Remembrance, and He placed it with Him above His Throne. Then He created the second pen to write with it on earth, as will be explained in the surah "Read in the name of your Lord" [[See vol. 20, p. 117]] [al-Alaq: 1].

His saying, the Exalted: "And what they inscribe" (wa ma yasturun): that is, what they write. He means the angels who write the deeds of the children of Adam; this is said by Ibn Abbas. It is also said: "and what they write," that is, people and what they convey to one another by it. Ibn Abbas also said: the meaning of "wa ma yasturun" is "and what they know." Ma may be a relative pronoun or a verbal-source particle: meaning either "and what they inscribe" or "and their inscribing," and it may refer to each one who inscribes or to the recording angels, according to the difference of opinion.

"You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman": this is the response to the oath, and it is a negation. The polytheists used to say to the Prophet ﷺ that he was mad, possessed by a jinn.

This is their saying: "O you to whom the Remembrance has been sent down, you are truly mad" [al-Hijr: 6]. So Allah, the Exalted, sent down in reply to them and in refutation of their saying: "You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman," that is, by the mercy of your Lord. The grace here is mercy. It is also possible that "by the grace" is an oath; its sense being: "You and the grace of your Lord are not mad," because the waw and the ba are particles of oath. It has also been said: it is like your saying: "You are not mad, and praise be to Allah." It has also been said: its meaning is "You are not mad, and the grace belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise," meaning "and praise belongs to Allah." From it is the saying of Labid:

"I was left alone in the world after the loss of my kinsfolk,
and a neighbour in Arbad, a beneficial one, departed from me."

That is, "and he is Arbad." Al-Nabigha said:

"They were not deprived of the goodness of nourishment, and their mother
overflowed upon you with a male-begetting milk-bag."

That is, "he is the one who bears." The ba in "by the grace of your Lord" is connected to "madman" negated, just as it is connected to "heedless" affirmed, as in your saying: "You are heedless of the grace of your Lord." Its position is accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), as if he said: "You are not mad, one who has been favoured with that."

"And indeed for you is a reward": that is, a recompense for what you have borne of the burdens of prophethood.

"Never cut off" (ghayra mamnun): that is, not cut off and not diminished. It is said: "I cut the rope" (mantu al-habl) when I severed it, and a rope is called "manin" when it is not strong. The poet said:

"grey, swift birds whose food is not cut off [[This is the second half of a line by Labid; its first half is disputed. See the root (m-t-n) in Lisan al-Arab. The ghubs is the colour of ashes.]]"

That is, is not cut off. Mujahid said: "never cut off" means "counted" (mahsub). Al-Hasan said: "never cut off" means not spoiled by reproach. Al-Dahhak said: a reward without work. It has also been said: "not measured," which is grace (al-tafaddul), because recompense is measured and grace is not measured; this was mentioned by al-Mawardi, and it is the meaning of Mujahid's saying.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 4:

There are two issues here.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed you are of a great character﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: "upon a great character", meaning upon a great religion among the religions; there is no religion more beloved to Allah, exalted is He, nor more pleasing to Him than it. In the Sahih of Muslim, from 'A'isha, that his character (khuluq) was the Qur'an. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and 'Atiyya said: it is the etiquette (adab) of the Qur'an. It was also said: it is his gentleness towards his community and his honouring of them. Qatada said: it is that he would carry out the commands of Allah and refrain from what Allah forbade. It was said: that is, you are upon a noble disposition (tab' karim). Al-Mawardi said: and this is the apparent meaning.

The linguistic reality of khuluq (character): it is the etiquette (adab) that a person imposes upon himself, and it is called khuluq because it becomes like a creation (khilqa) in him. As for the etiquette one is naturally disposed to, it is called al-khiim (with a kasra): innate disposition and natural temperament, which has no singular form from its own wording. Khiim is also the name of a mountain. Thus khuluq is the acquired disposition, and al-khiim is the instinctive natural temperament. Al-A'sha clarified this in his poetry, saying:

"And when the one of bounties withholds from the wealth, and characters return to their khiim (natural dispositions)"

That is, characters returned to their natural dispositions.

I say: what I have mentioned from 'A'isha in the Sahih of Muslim is the most authentic of the sayings. I was also asked about his character, peace be upon him, so she recited ﴿Successful indeed are the believers﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1] up to ten verses, and said: No one had a better character than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever any of the Companions or of his family called him, he would say, "Labbayk" (I am at your service). That is why Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed you are of a great character﴾. No praiseworthy character is mentioned except that the Prophet (ﷺ) had the largest share of it.

Al-Junayd said: his character was called great because no aspiration of his was other than Allah, exalted is He. It was also said his character was called great because the noble qualities of character were gathered in him, as shown by his peace be upon him saying: "Indeed Allah sent me to perfect the noble qualities of character." It was also said: because he complied with Allah's discipline of him in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is customary, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199]. It has been related from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "My Lord disciplined me with an excellent discipline when He said: ﴿Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is customary, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199]; and when I accepted that from Him, He said: ﴿And indeed you are of a great character﴾."

The second: al-Tirmidhi related from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow an evil deed with a good deed, and it will erase it, and deal with people with good character." He said: a hasan sahih hadith. And from Abu al-Darda': that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is heavier in the scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection than good character, and indeed Allah hates the foul-mouthed and obscene." He said: a hasan sahih hadith. And from him, he said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Nothing placed in the scale is heavier than good character, and indeed the person of good character reaches by it the rank of the one who prays and fasts." He said: a gharib hadith from this route. And from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about what most admits people into Paradise? He said: "Taqwa of Allah and good character." And he was asked about what most admits people into the Fire? He said: "The mouth and the private parts." He said: this is a sahih gharib hadith. And from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, who described good character, saying: it is cheerfulness of face, giving of what is good, and restraining harm. And from Jabir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed among you the most beloved to me and the closest to me in sitting on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character," and he said: "And indeed the most hateful to me among you and the farthest from me in sitting on the Day of Resurrection are the thartharun, the mutashaddiqun, and the mutafayhiqun." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we know the thartharun and the mutashaddiqun, so what are the mutafayhiqun?" He said: "The arrogant." He said: and in the chapter from Abu Hurayra; and this is a hasan gharib hadith from this route.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 5–7:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is "so you will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection." It was also said: "so you will see and they will see on the Day of Resurrection, when truth and falsehood become distinct."

(﴿Which of you is the afflicted one﴾) The "bi" (ba') is extra (za'idah, redundant); that is, "so you will see and they will see which of you is the afflicted one." Al-Maftun is the one who has been afflicted with madness, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai, yielding oil﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 20] and ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. This is the view of Qatadah, Abu 'Ubayd and al-Akhfash. The rajiz (rajaz poet) said:

"We are the sons of Ja'dah, the companions of al-Falaj...
we strike with the sword and hope for relief."

[Al-Falaj (with a fatha on the fa' and the lam): a town in the land of al-Yamamah belonging to the Banu Ja'dah. It is also permissible to say: "nahnu banu..." in the accusative, by way of specification (al-ikhtisas).

(See the eighty-ninth witness after the seven hundredth in Khizanat al-Adab.)]

It was also said: the "ba'" is not extra, and the meaning is: "which of you is the afflicted one," that is, the affliction (al-fitnah). This is a verbal noun (masdar) on the pattern of the passive participle, and its meaning is al-futun (the affliction), as they say: "there is no majlud (flogging) or ma'qul (reason) for so-and-so," meaning no reason and no endurance. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Ra'i said:

"Until, when they left for his bones no flesh, nor for his heart any ma'qul (reason)."

That is, no reason ('aqlan). It was also said that there is an omitted genitive construction in the sentence, and the meaning is: "which of you is the affliction of the afflicted one." Al-Farra' said: the "ba'" here means "fi" (in), that is, "so you will see and they will see in which of the two groups is the madman: is it the group you are in, the believers, or the other group?" Al-Maftun is the madman whom the devil has afflicted. It was also said: al-maftun means the one who is punished, from the Arabic saying: "I afflicted (fatantu) the gold with fire" when you heat it. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the Day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], that is, they will be punished. Most of the surah was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Abu Jahl. It was also said: al-maftun is the devil, because he is afflicted in his religion. They used to say: "Indeed, in him is a devil," and by "the madman" they meant this. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will surely know tomorrow which of them is the madman﴾, that is, the devil from whose touch madness and confusion of the intellect arise.

(﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾) That is, indeed Allah is the Knower of those who have deviated from His religion.

(﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾) That is, those who are upon guidance, so that He will recompense each one tomorrow according to his deeds.

He forbade him from *mumayalat* (yielding to or flattering) the polytheists. They had been asking him to stop opposing them so that they would stop opposing him. So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that this is a form of disbelief that *yaltahim* (yields to) kufr. Allah, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And had We not given you firmness, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. [[See vol. 10, p. 300]]

It was also said: meaning, do not obey the deniers in what they call you to of their wicked religion. It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh when they called him to the religion of his forefathers.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 9:

Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtiyyah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "They wish that you would disbelieve, so that they would persist in their disbelief." It is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: "They wish that you would grant them concessions, so that they would grant you concessions." Al-Farra' and al-Kalbi said: "[They wish] that you would be lenient, so that they would be lenient toward you." Al-Idhan (ʾidhān, here: softening, flattery) means softening toward one who does not deserve softening; this was said by al-Farra'. Mujahid said: The meaning is, "They wish that you would incline toward them and abandon the truth, so that they would side with you." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They wish that you would lie, so that they would lie." Qatadah said: "They wish that you would turn away from this matter, so that they would turn away with you." Al-Hasan said: "They wish that you would make accommodations to them in your religion, so that they would make accommodations to you in their religion." And from him also: "They wish that you would abandon some of your command, so that they would abandon some of their command." Zayd ibn Aslam: "[They wish] that you would be hypocritical and show off, so that they would be hypocritical and show off." It has also been said: "They wish that you would weaken, so that they would weaken," said by Abu Jaʿfar. It has also been said: "They wish that you would compromise (tudahin) in your religion, so that they would compromise in their religions," said by al-Qutabi. And from him: they asked him to worship their gods for a period, and they would worship his God for a period.

So these are twelve opinions. Ibn al-ʿArabi said: The commentators have mentioned about ten opinions regarding it, all of them claims about the language and the meaning. The best of them is their saying: "They wish that you would lie, so that they would lie," and "They wish that you would disbelieve, so that they would disbelieve."

I say: All of them, God willing, are correct according to the requirements of the language and the meaning, for al-Idhan (al-idhān, here: flattery) is softness and accommodation. It has also been said: it is courting an enemy and inclining toward him. It has also been said: approximation in speech and softness in words. The poet said:

"Some of the foolish are more prudent in matters
that befall you, than the flattery of the enemy."

Al-Mufaddal said: it is hypocrisy and abandoning sincere advice. On this sense it is blameworthy, and on the first sense it is not blameworthy, and each of them did not occur. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said "idhan fi dinihi" and "dahana fi amrihi," meaning he betrayed in it and displayed the opposite of what he concealed. Some people said: "dahana" in the sense of "warra" (concealed), and "adhana" in the sense of "ghashsha" (deceived), said by al-Jawhari. He said: "fa-yudhinun" he (God) placed it in the form of coordination (ʿatf), and had it been a response to the prohibition he would have said "fa-yudhinu." What is meant is: if they wish that you would do [such and such], then they would do the like of your act, as coordination with no requital upon it and no reciprocation; it is rather an illustration and a parallel.

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 68, verses 10–13:

He means al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, according to al-Sha'bi, al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq. It is also said that he is al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, or Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad; this was said by Mujahid. It is also said that he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who offered the Prophet ﷺ wealth and swore that he would give it to him if he turned away from his religion; this was said by Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said: he is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

*Al-hallaf* means one who swears often. *Al-mahin* means the weak of heart, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: it means the liar, and the liar is contemptible. It is also said: one who persists in evil; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Al-Kalbi said: *al-mahin* is the wicked, the incapable. It is also said that its meaning is one who is despised by Allah. Ibn Shajarah said: it means the humiliated. Al-Rummani said: *al-mahin* is the base, lowly one, because of his abundance of ugliness. It is a *fa'il* form derived from *al-mahanah*, meaning lowness, and here it means lack of judgment and discernment. Or it is a *fa'il* form with the meaning of *maf'il*, so the meaning is one who is humiliated.

(*Hammaz*) Ibn Zayd said: *al-hammaz* is one who strikes people with his hand and beats them, while *al-lammaz* is one who does so with his tongue. Al-Hasan said: it is one who gestures with the head or eye at someone in a gathering, like the verse: ﴿Woe to every backbiter and slanderer﴾ [al-Humazah 104:1]. It is also said: *al-hammaz* is one who insults people to their faces, and *al-lammaz* is one who slanders them behind their backs; this was said by Abu al-Aliyah, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and also al-Hasan. Muqatil said the opposite of this: *al-humazah* is one who backbites in absence, and *al-lumazah* is one who defames to the face. Murrah said: the two are the same. And it is the one who spreads tales and slanders a man when he is absent; this is similar to what is reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The poet said:

*You show affection when you meet me, but with lies,*
*and when I am absent, you are the one who defames and slanders.*

(*Mashsha'in bi-namim*) That is, one who walks about carrying tale-bearing among people in order to cause discord between them. It is said: *namma yanummu namman, wa namiman, wa namimah*, meaning he walks about and goes about spreading corruption. In Sahih Muslim, it is reported from Hudhayfah that he was told that a man was carrying tales, so Hudhayfah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The one who carries tales will not enter Paradise." The poet said:

Verses 14–15: "Because he has wealth and sons."

Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, Abu Haywa, al-Mughira and al-A'raj read "آنَ كَانَ" with a single lengthened hamza, as an interrogative. Al-Mufaddal, Abu Bakr and Hamza read "أَأَنْ كَانَ" with two clearly articulated hamzas. The rest read it with a single hamza as a statement. Whoever reads with a lengthened single hamza or with two clear hamzas makes it an interrogative, meant as a rebuke. It is good for the reader to pause at "zanim" (base-born) and then begin with "أَنْ كَانَ," with the meaning: "Is it because he has wealth and sons that you obey him?" It is also possible that the sense is: "Is it because he has wealth and sons that, when Our verses are recited to him, he says: 'The fables of the ancients!'?" It is also possible that the sense is: "Is it because he has wealth and sons that he disbelieves and is arrogant?" What came before in the speech indicates this, so it is as if it were stated after the interrogative.

As for whoever reads "أَنْ كَانَ" without an interrogative, it is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), and its governing verb is an implied verb. The sense is: "He disbelieves because he has wealth and sons." What indicates this verb is "When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'The fables of the ancients.'" The word "تُتْلَى" does not govern "أَنْ," nor does "قَالَ," because what follows "إِذَا" does not govern what precedes it, since "إِذَا" is attached to the clauses that follow it, and the genitive-attached word does not govern what precedes the thing it is attached to. "قَالَ" is the answer of the conditional, and the answer to a conditional does not govern what precedes the conditional; the governing element ought to come before the governed element, whereas the answer to a condition must come after the condition, so it becomes in one respect placed before and in another after.

It is also possible that the meaning is: "Do not obey him because he is wealthy and numerous."

Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever reads without an interrogative, it is not good to pause at "zanim," because the meaning is "because he was" and "that he was," so "أَنْ" is connected to what precedes it. Others said: it may be connected to his words "مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ" (going about with slander), with the sense: "he walks about with slander because he has wealth and sons." Abu 'Ali permitted its connection to "عُتُلٍّ" (brutal).

"Asatir al-awwalin" means their falsehoods, their nonsense, and their fabrications. [In the originals: "وخراريقهم" with a qaf.] And this has already been discussed [see vol. 6, p. 054].

**Question one.** Allah's words: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: The meaning of "sanasimuhu" (We will brand him) is "sanakhtimuhu bi-al-sayf" (We will mark his nose with the sword). He said: The man concerning whom this was revealed was struck on the nose with the sword on the day of Badr, and he remained with a mark on his nose until he died.

Qatadah said: "sanasimuhu" means that on the Day of Resurrection there will be a mark on his nose by which he is recognized. It is said: "wasamtuhu wasman wasimah" when one leaves an impression on him with a brand or cautery. Allah has said: ﴿On the Day when some faces turn white and some faces turn black﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106]. This is a clear sign. And Allah has said: ﴿And We will gather the criminals on that Day, blue-eyed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102]. This is another clear sign. This verse therefore adds a third sign, which is branding on the nose with fire. This is like His words: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾ [al-Rahman: 41]. This was said by al-Kalbi and others.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Mujahid said: "sanasimuhu 'ala al-khurtum" means upon his snout, that is, upon his nose, and "We will blacken his face in the Hereafter, so he will be recognized by the blackness of his face." Al-khurtum is the nose of a human being. Among beasts of prey, it is the place of the lip. "Kharatim al-qawm" means their leaders. Al-Farra' said: Although al-khurtum is specifically associated with the brand, it carries the sense of the face, because a part of a thing may be used to express the whole.

Al-Tabari said: We will make his matter clear in a manifest way, so that they will recognize it and it will not be hidden from them, just as a brand is not hidden on the snouts.

It has also been said: The meaning is, "We will attach to him a disgrace and an insult, until he becomes like one who has been branded on his nose." Al-Qutaybi said: The Arabs say of a man who is reviled with a shameful and lasting insult, "He has been branded with a brand of evil," meaning that a disgrace has been affixed to him that will not leave him, just as the trace of a brand is not erased. Jarir said:

*When I placed my brand upon al-Farazdaq,*
*and upon al-Ba'ith [1] I slit the nose of al-Akhtal.*

He meant by this satire.

He said: All of this was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. We do not know of any case in which Allah has mentioned the defects of anyone to a greater extent than He did with him, attaching to him a disgrace that will not leave him in this world or the next, like the branding on the snout.

It has also been said: It refers to what Allah afflicted him with in this world, in his person, his wealth and his family, of evil, humiliation and abasement. This was said by Ibn Bahr, who cited the words of al-A'sha:

*So leave her, and what concerns you; aim for another*
*with your poetry, and mark [2] the nose of whoever you are and whoever you are.*

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The meaning is, "We will flog him for drinking wine." Al-khurtum means wine, and its plural is kharatim. The poet said:

*You spend your day in amusement and in merriment,*
*and at night you are a drinker of the kharatim.*

The rajaz poet [3] said:

*Tawny, khurtuman, strong, and pungent [4]*

And another said:

*Abu Hadir, whoever commits fornication will be known by his fornication,*
*and whoever drinks the khurtum will wake up intoxicated.*

**Question two.** Ibn al-'Arabi said: In ancient times, branding the face of a person guilty of sin was known among people, to the extent that it has been narrated, as already mentioned, that the Jews, when they neglected stoning the adulterer, substituted beating him and blackening his face. This is a false practice. Among the valid forms of branding on the face is what the scholars have seen in blackening the face of a false witness, as a sign of the ugliness of the sin and as a deterrent to others who would engage in it, by the punishment and notoriety that a false witness may hope to face. He was honored for speaking the truth, and he has become debased through sin. The greatest humiliation is the humiliation of the face. Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verses 20–22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So it became like a Sarim﴾, i.e., like the pitch-dark night, related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Farra' and others. The poet said:

"Your night has stretched out, black and dark, / so it does not part from a dark morning" [[In al-Lisan, under the root ṣ-r-m:

"So it does not part from a black night"]], i.e., it was burned and became like the blackest night.

And also from Ibn 'Abbas: like black ash. He said: al-Sarim is black ash in the dialect of Khuzaymah. al-Thawri said: like a harvested field, so al-Sarim here means the mashrum (the cut-off), i.e., that from which the produce has been cut. al-Hasan said: its good was cut off from it (ṣurima 'anha al-khayr), i.e., it was cut off, so al-Sarim is also a passive participle. al-Mu'arrij said: i.e., like a sand-dune that has been cut off from the main body of sand. It is said: ṣarīmah and ṣarā'im. So a sand-dune produces nothing from which benefit can be gained. al-Akhfash said: i.e., like the morning that has been cut off from the night. al-Mubarrad said: i.e., like the day, in which there is nothing. Shamir said: al-Sarim is the night and al-Sarim is the day, meaning that one is cut off from the other and the other from this one. It has also been said: the night was called sarim because its darkness cuts off activity (yaqta' bi-zulmatihi 'an al-tasarruf), and for this reason it is of the form fa'il in the sense of fa'il (active). al-Qushayri said: there is room to examine this, because the day is also called sarim, and it does not cut off activity.

Then it was said: the right that the poor people of the garden were denied may have been obligatory upon them, or it may have been voluntary; the first is more apparent, and God knows best. This has already been discussed, meaning: indeed, for the righteous in the Hereafter are gardens in which there is only pure enjoyment, unmixed with anything that spoils it, as the gardens of this world are mixed with it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are gardens of bliss﴾. This has already been discussed, meaning: indeed, for the righteous in the Hereafter are gardens in which there is only pure enjoyment, unmixed with anything that spoils it, as the gardens of this world are mixed with it. When they heard talk of the Hereafter and what Allah had promised the believers, they said: "If it is true that we will be resurrected as Muhammad and those with him claim, then our state and theirs will be no different from what it is in this world. Otherwise, they will not have more than us or be superior to us, and at best they will be equal to us." So Allah said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾, meaning, like the disbelievers. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: The disbelievers of Makkah said: "We will be given better in the Hereafter than what you are given," so this was revealed: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾. How do you judge?﴾, meaning this crooked judgment, as if the matter of recompense were entrusted to you so that you could judge in it as you wish, that you would have the same good as the Muslims.

﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study?﴾, meaning: do you have a Book in which you find the obedient treated like the disobedient?

Ibn Kaysan said: al-za'im here is the one who establishes the proof and the claim. Al-Hasan said: al-za'im is the Messenger.

(Am lahum shuraka'): meaning, do they have them? The mim is an added particle (silah). Shuraka' means witnesses.

(Fal-ya'tu bi-shuraka'ihim): let them bring their partners to testify to what they claimed.

(In kanu sadiqin): their claim, if they are truthful. It has also been said: meaning, let them bring their partners if they are able to, and this is a command whose meaning is to render them powerless (al-ta'jiz).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 42–43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when a shin is laid bare﴾. It is permissible for the governing element (al-'amil) of "yawma" (on the day) to be "fal-ya'tu" (then let them bring), meaning: then let them bring their partners, on the day when a shin is laid bare, so that the partners may intercede for them. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: remember the day when a shin is laid bare. In this case the pause is made at ﴿sadiqin﴾ (truthful), and it is not paused on it under the first interpretation.

It has been read as "yawma nakshifu" with the nun. Ibn 'Abbas read "yawma takshifu 'an saqin" with the ta' of the masculine (the verb with a feminine subject), meaning: the hardship, or the Resurrection, lays bare its shin, as in their saying: "shammarat al-harbu 'an saqiha" (the war rolled up its shin). The poet said:

A youth of war: if war bites him, he bites it back, and if war rolls up its shin, he rolls up (his sleeves).[[The line is by Hatim al-Ta'i. It is also transmitted as: "akhu al-harb" and "akha al-harb".]]

And the rajiz said:

It has bared its shin, so gird yourselves, and war has become serious with you, so be serious.

And another said:

I marvel at myself and at its fear, and at the chasing of birds from their provisions,
in a year that has bared its shin, red, stripping the flesh from its bones.[[al-'uraq with a dammah on the ayn: the bone without flesh; if it still has flesh on it, it is 'irq with a fatha.]]

And another said:

It bared to them its shin, and the evident evil appeared.

And from Ibn 'Abbas also, al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah read "tukshafu" with the ta' of the non-named subject (passive). This reading refers back to the meaning of yukshafu, as if he had said: on the day when the Resurrection is laid bare of a hardship.

It has been read as "yawma tukshifu" with a ta' that is damma and a kasra on the shin, from aksafa, meaning he entered into the state of being laid bare. From this: "aksafa al-rajulu fa-huwa muksaf," when his upper lip has been turned back.

Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned, saying: Usamah ibn Zayd informed us from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, may He be exalted: "On the day when a shin is laid bare," he said: "from distress and hardship." Ibn Jurayj informed us from Mujahid, who said: "the severity of the matter and its seriousness." Mujahid said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "it is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection." Abu 'Ubaydah said: when war or a matter becomes intense, it is said: "the matter was laid bare of its shin." The origin of this is that whoever falls into a matter that requires exertion rolls up his shin, so the shin and its uncovering are borrowed for a place of hardship. It was also said: the shin of a thing is its root upon which its stability rests, like the trunk of a tree or the shin of a person, meaning: on the day when the root of the matter is laid bare, and the realities of affairs and their origins become manifest. It was also said: it is laid bare from the shin of Hell. It was also said: from the shin of the Throne. It was also said: it refers to the time of the approach of the end and the weakness of the body, meaning: the sick person uncovers his shin to see his weakness, and the muezzin calls him to prayer, but he cannot stand and go out. As for what has been related, that Allah uncovers His shin, He, may He be exalted, is far above limbs and division, and above uncovering and covering. Its meaning is that He uncovers the greatness of His affair. It was also said: He uncovers His light, may He be mighty and majestic. Abu Musa related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying, "from a shin," that he said: "He uncovers a great light, and they fall down before Him in prostration."

Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi said in his tafsir: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Hudbah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Zayd, from 'Umarah al-Qurashi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: my father narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, every people will be shown what they used to worship in the world, and every people goes off to what they used to worship, and those of monotheism remain. It is said to them: What are you waiting for, when the people have gone? They say: Indeed we have a Lord whom we used to worship in the world, and we did not see Him. He said: And will you recognise Him if you see Him? They say: Yes. It is said: How will you recognise Him when you have not seen Him? They say: Indeed He has no likeness. So He uncovers the veil for them, and they look at Allah, may He be exalted, and fall down before Him in prostration. And there remain groups whose backs are like the horns (siyasi) of cattle.[[Siyasi al-baqar: their horns.]] They look at Allah, may He be exalted, and wish to prostrate, but they cannot. That is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the day when a shin is laid bare﴾, and they are called to prostration but they are unable. Then Allah, may He be exalted, says: O My servants, raise your heads, for I have made in place of every man among you a man from the Jews and the Christians in the Fire." Abu Burdah said: I related this hadith to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, and he said: By Allah, besides whom there is no god, did your father truly narrate this hadith to you? So he swore to him three oaths. 'Umar said: I have not heard about the people of monotheism a hadith more beloved to me than this one.

Qays ibn al-Sakan said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud related in the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot and naked, the sweat bridling them. Allah does not speak to them, nor does He look at them, for forty years. Then a caller calls: O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, shaped you, caused you to die, gave you life, and then you worshipped other than Him, that He should turn each people to what they turned to? They say: Yes. He says: Then there is raised for each people what they used to worship besides Allah, and they follow it until it casts them into the Fire. The Muslims and the hypocrites remain, and it is said to them: Will you not go? The people have gone. They say: Until our Lord comes to us. It is said to them: Or do you recognise Him? They say: If He describes Himself to us, we will recognise Him. [[i.e., if He describes Himself with an attribute by which He is known.]] He said: At that moment a shin is laid bare, and He manifests Himself to them, and whoever used to worship Him sincerely falls down in prostration, while the hypocrites remain unable, as if in their backs were spits (safafid),[[al-safafid: plural of al-safud (the form of tannur): the iron rod on which meat is roasted.]] and they are taken away to the Fire, while these enter Paradise. That is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they are called to prostration but they are unable.﴾

﴿Humbled their eyes﴾ meaning: abased, humbled; its accusative is as a circumstantial state (hal).

﴿Degradation will cover them﴾. That is because the believers raise their heads and faces, whiter than snow, while the faces of the hypocrites and the disbelievers blacken until they return blacker than pitch. I say: the meaning of the hadith of Abu Musa and Ibn Mas'ud is established in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and others.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾, meaning: in the world.

(﴿while they were sound﴾) — healthy, free from affliction. Ibrahim al-Taymi said: meaning they are called by the adhan and the iqamah, but they refuse it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they would hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) and would not respond. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was only revealed concerning those who lag behind from the congregations. It was also said: meaning by the obligation laid upon them in the Shari'ah, and the meaning is close. The discussion on the obligation of congregational prayer has passed in Surah al-Baqarah.[[See vol. 1, p. 348.]] Al-Rabi' ibn Khaytham had become paralysed, and he was helped along between two men to the mosque, so it was said: O Abu Yazid, if you prayed in your house you would have a concession. He said: Whoever hears "Hasten to success," let him respond, even crawling. It was said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Tariq wants to kill you, so hide yourself. He said: Where Allah cannot reach me? It was said to him: Sit in your house. He said: I hear "Hasten to success," and I do not respond!

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 44–45:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Leave Me﴾ means: leave Me (dha'nī, "leave Me to Myself").

(And whoever denies) "man" is either in the accusative as an object accompanied by (maf'ul ma'ahu, the object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the pronoun of the speaker (ma'tuf 'ala damir al-mutakallim).

(this Discourse) means the Qur'an, as said by al-Suddi. It was also said: (it refers to) the Day of Resurrection. This is a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: so I will requite them and take vengeance upon them. Then He said: (﴿We shall draw them step by step from where they do not know﴾). Its meaning: We shall seize them unawares while they do not perceive, so they were punished on the Day of Badr. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We shower blessings upon them and make them forget gratitude. Al-Hasan said: How many are led on step by step through kindness shown to them, how many are beguiled by praise bestowed on them, and how many are deceived by being concealed (from their sins). Abu Rawq said: that is, whenever they commit a sin, We renew a blessing for them and make them forget seeking forgiveness. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We will plot against them." It was also said: it means that We take them gradually and do not seize them suddenly. And in a hadith: "A man from the Children of Israel said: 'O Lord, how often shall I disobey You while You do not punish me?' — He said — So God revealed to the prophet of their time: Tell him, how many punishments of Mine there are upon you while you are unaware. Indeed, the stiffness of your eyes and the hardness of your heart are a step-by-step leading (istidraj) from Me and a punishment, if only you understood."

Istidraj (gradual leading on, inducing a person step by step toward ruin): the leaving off of hastening. Its root is transfer from one state to another, like tadarruj (gradual progression). From it comes the word daraja (degree), which is a station after another station. Istadraja fulan fulanan means: he drew out from him what he had, little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha and istadrajahu have the same meaning, i.e., he brought him near to it gradually, so he progressed (tadarraja) himself.

(And I give them respite) means: I grant them time and lengthen their term. Al-Mulawa (the period of time; its mim may be vowelled in three ways) is a span of time. Allah amla lahu means He lengthened it for him. Al-Malawan are the night and the day. It was also said: (﴿And I give them respite﴾) means I do not hasten them with death; the meaning is the same. This has already been explained in "al-A'raf".

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 44–45:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Leave Me﴾ means: leave Me (dha'nī, "leave Me to Myself").

(And whoever denies) "man" is either in the accusative as an object accompanied by (maf'ul ma'ahu, the object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the pronoun of the speaker (ma'tuf 'ala damir al-mutakallim).

(this Discourse) means the Qur'an, as said by al-Suddi. It was also said: (it refers to) the Day of Resurrection. This is a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: so I will requite them and take vengeance upon them. Then He said: (﴿We shall draw them step by step from where they do not know﴾). Its meaning: We shall seize them unawares while they do not perceive, so they were punished on the Day of Badr. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We shower blessings upon them and make them forget gratitude. Al-Hasan said: How many are led on step by step through kindness shown to them, how many are beguiled by praise bestowed on them, and how many are deceived by being concealed (from their sins). Abu Rawq said: that is, whenever they commit a sin, We renew a blessing for them and make them forget seeking forgiveness. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We will plot against them." It was also said: it means that We take them gradually and do not seize them suddenly. And in a hadith: "A man from the Children of Israel said: 'O Lord, how often shall I disobey You while You do not punish me?' — He said — So God revealed to the prophet of their time: Tell him, how many punishments of Mine there are upon you while you are unaware. Indeed, the stiffness of your eyes and the hardness of your heart are a step-by-step leading (istidraj) from Me and a punishment, if only you understood."

Istidraj (gradual leading on, inducing a person step by step toward ruin): the leaving off of hastening. Its root is transfer from one state to another, like tadarruj (gradual progression). From it comes the word daraja (degree), which is a station after another station. Istadraja fulan fulanan means: he drew out from him what he had, little by little. It is said: darajahu ila kadha and istadrajahu have the same meaning, i.e., he brought him near to it gradually, so he progressed (tadarraja) himself.

(And I give them respite) means: I grant them time and lengthen their term. Al-Mulawa (the period of time; its mim may be vowelled in three ways) is a span of time. Allah amla lahu means He lengthened it for him. Al-Malawan are the night and the day. It was also said: (﴿And I give them respite﴾) means I do not hasten them with death; the meaning is the same. This has already been explained in "al-A'raf".

(﴿Indeed My plan is firm﴾) means: indeed My punishment is strong and severe, so none escapes Me.

The discourse returns to what preceded in His saying, exalted is He: "Or do they have partners?" (al-Qalam 68:41). That is: "Or are you seeking from them a reward for what you call them to of faith in Allah? So they are burdened by the penalty of that, because it would be hard for them to give up wealth." That is, there is no hardship upon them; rather, by following you they would gain mastery over the treasures of the earth and reach the Gardens of Bliss.

"Or do they have the unseen, so that they write (it down)?" He said: that is, the knowledge of what is hidden from them.

(So they write.) It was also said: Is the revelation sent down to them with this which they say? It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that al-ghayb here means the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so they write from what is in it, by which they dispute with you, and they write that they are better than you, and that they will not be punished. It was also said: "yaktubun" means they judge in their own favour by whatever they wish.

"The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord﴾, that is, for the decree of your Lord. Here "al-hukm" means al-qada' (the decree). It was also said: "Be patient with what your Lord has decreed for you of conveying the Message." Ibn Bahr said: "Be patient for the victory of your Lord." Qatadah said: "That is, do not hasten and do not become angry, for your support will certainly come." It was also said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

(﴿And be not like the companion of the fish﴾) meaning Yunus (peace be upon him), that is, do not be like him in anger, impatience and haste. Qatadah said: Allah Exalted consoles His Prophet (ﷺ), commanding him to be patient and not to hasten as the companion of the fish hastened. His story has already passed in Surat Yunus, [see vol. 8 p. 383], and in al-Anbiya', [see vol. 11 p. 239], and in as-Saffat [see vol. 15 p. 121]. The difference between the idafah of dhu and sahib in Surat Yunus, so there is no point in repeating it.

(﴿When he called out﴾) that is, when he called out from within the belly of the fish, saying: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87].

(﴿while he was suppressing [his grief]﴾) that is, filled with distress. It was also said: "in anguish." The first is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid; the second is the statement of 'Ata' and Abu Malik. Al-Mawardi said: The difference between them is that ghamm is in the heart, while karb is in the breath. It was also said: "makzum" means "confined," and al-kazm means restraint, from which comes their saying: "So-and-so suppressed his rage (kazama ghaydahu)," that is, he restrained his anger. This was said by Ibn Bahr. It was also said: it refers to one who is seized by his throat (kazm), which is the passage of breath, as said by al-Mubarrad. This and other matters have already passed in "Yusuf" [see vol. 9 p. 259].

﴿لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾: The common reading (qira'at al-'amma) is *tadarakahu* (تَدارَكَهُ). Ibn Hurmuz and al-Hasan read *taddarakahu* (تَدَّارَكُهُ), with the *dal* doubled. This is a present-tense form in which the *ta'* has been assimilated into the *dal*, and it is to be understood as a narration of the state (*hikayat al-hal*), as if he had said: "Were it not that there would be said of him, 'a blessing from his Lord would overtake him'." Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud read *tadarakthu* (تَدارَكَتْهُ), which goes against the written text (*al-marsum*, the consonantal script of the Qur'an). The verb *tadarakahu* is a masculine past-tense form, which is construed according to the sense of *ni'ma* (blessing), since the feminine gender of *ni'ma* is not a true feminine. *Tadarakthu* follows its wording.

The scholars differ on the meaning of *ni'ma* here. It is said to be prophethood; this was said by al-Dahhak. It is said to be his former worship; this was said by Ibn Jubayr. It is said to be his supplication, *﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾* [al-Anbiya: 87]; this was said by Ibn Zayd. It is said to be God's blessing upon him in bringing him out of the belly of the fish; this was said by Ibn Bahr. It is also said: that is, a mercy from his Lord, so He had mercy on him and accepted his repentance.

﴿لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ﴾: That is, he would have been cast out as one blamed, but he was cast out sick and not blameworthy. The meaning of *madhmum* (blamed) in the words of Ibn 'Abbas is *mulim* (one who has committed a blameworthy act). Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *mudhnib* (sinner). It is also said: *madhmum* means one who is distanced from every good. *Al-'ara'* is the wide open plain, in which there is no mountain or tree to give cover. It is also said: Had it not been for God's grace upon him, he would have remained in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection, and then he would have been cast out onto the plain of the Resurrection as one blamed. Evidence for this is His saying, Exalted is He: *﴿فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ * لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾* [al-Saffat: 143–144]. (See vol. 15, p. 123.)

﴿فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: That is, He chose him and preferred him. ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: God returned revelation to him, interceded for him regarding himself and his people, accepted his repentance, and made him among the righteous by sending him to a hundred thousand or more.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 68, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip﴾. Inna (indeed) here is the lightened form (al-mukhaffafah) of the heavy inna. Layuzliqunaka means: they would afflict you with the evil eye (ya'taninaka).

(bi-absarihim) He informed of the intensity of their enmity toward the Prophet (ﷺ), and they wanted to strike him with the evil eye. A group of the Quraysh looked at him and said: "We have never seen the like of him, nor the like of his proofs." It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banu Asad, to the extent that a fat cow or a fat she-camel would pass by one of them, he would gaze at it, then say: "O girl, take the basket [[al-mikta: a basket made of palm fronds in which dates and other things are carried.]] and the dirham, and bring us the meat of this she-camel," and it would not leave until it fell dead and was slaughtered. Al-Kalbi said: a man of the Arabs would remain for two or three days without eating anything, then he would raise the side of the tent, and camels or sheep would pass by him, and he would say: "I have not seen today any camels or sheep better than these!" and they would not go far before a group of them would fall dead. So the disbelievers asked this man to strike the Prophet (ﷺ) with the evil eye for them, and he agreed. When the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by, he recited:

Your people used to reckon you a lord... and I think you are a bewitched lord.

So Allah protected His Prophet (ﷺ), and the verse was revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip﴾. Al-Mawardi mentioned something similar. And the Arabs, when one of them wanted to strike someone, meaning in his person or property, would go hungry for three days, then he would expose himself and his property and say: "By Allah, I have never seen anyone stronger than him, nor braver, nor more numerous, nor more beautiful," and he would strike him with his eye, and he and his property would perish. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. Al-Qushayri said: there is a point to examine here, because striking with the evil eye occurs only with admiration and approval, not with aversion and hatred. Therefore He said: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is a madman"﴾, meaning they ascribe madness to you when they see you reciting the Quran. I say: the sayings of the exegetes and the lexicographers indicate what we have mentioned, and that their intent by looking at him was to kill him. Aversion to a thing does not prevent it from being struck by the evil eye out of enmity until it perishes. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Abu Wa'il and Mujahid read layuzliqunaka, meaning layuhlikunaka (to destroy you). This is a reading according to the interpretation, from zahaqat nafsuhu and azhaqaha (his soul departed and he caused it to depart). The people of Medina read (layazliqunaka) with a fathah on the ya', while the rest read it with a dammah, and both are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said: zalaqahu yazliquhu and azlaqahu yuzliquhu izlaqan, if he moved him away and removed him. And zalaqa ra'sahu yazliquhu zalqan, if he shaved it. Likewise azlaqahu and zalqahu tazliqan. A man who is zalaq and zumlaq (on the pattern of hudabid) and zumaliq and zummalaq (with a doubled mim), who ejaculates before intercourse, is reported by al-Jawhari and others. Thus the meaning of the word is removal and displacement, and that does not happen with regard to the Prophet (ﷺ) except by his destruction and death. Al-Harawi said: he meant they would afflict you with their eyes, removing you from your station where Allah established you, out of enmity toward you. Ibn Abbas said: they would pierce you with their eyes; it is said zalaqa al-sahm and zahaqa when the arrow passed through, and this is the saying of Mujahid, meaning they would pierce you from the intensity of their gaze. Al-Kalbi said: they would throw you down. And from him also, as well as al-Suddi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the message. Al-Awfi said: they would hurl you. Al-Mu'arrij said: they would remove you. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash said: they would test you. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: they would look at you with a sidelong glance of intense staring. Ibn Zayd said: they would touch you. Ja'far al-Sadiq said: they would devour you. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: they would kill you. This is like the saying: "he threw me down with his glance" and "he killed me with his eye." The poet said:

The one with the slipping eyes strikes you with its glance, and the arrows of the archer fall short of you.

Another said:

They exchange glances when they meet in a gathering, a glance that makes the feet slip from their places.

It was said: the meaning is that they look at you with enmity until they nearly bring you down. All of this returns to what we have mentioned, and the comprehensive meaning is: they would strike you with the evil eye. And Allah knows best.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is nothing but a reminder to the worlds. It was also said: meaning, Muhammad is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, by which they are reminded. It was also said: its meaning is honour (sharaf), i.e. the Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44] [[see vol. 16, p. 99]]. And the Prophet (ﷺ) is also an honour for the worlds: they were honoured by following him and believing in him (ﷺ)."
